questions.question: Which of the following is the coding of data so that it cannot be easily understood if intercepted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Encryption__

 
• Encryption is a way of scrambling data so that only authorized parties can understand the information. In technical terms, it is the process of converting plaintext to ciphertext. In simpler terms, encryption takes readable data and alters it so that it appears random. Encryption requires the use of an encryption key: a set of mathematical values that both the sender and the recipient of an encrypted message know.
 
• Although encrypted data appears random, encryption proceeds in a logical, predictable way, so that a party receiving the encrypted data and in possession of the key used to encrypt the data can decrypt the data, turning it back into plaintext. Truly secure encryption will be complex enough that a third party is highly unlikely to decrypt the ciphertext by brute force – in other words, by guessing.
 
• Data can be encrypted "at rest," when it is stored, or "in transit," while it is being transmitted somewhere else.

questions.question: A hard disk is divided into tracks which are further subdivided into:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sectors.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tracks are frequently used to split the surfaces into concentric rings. Sectors are used to split tracks.
 
• On a disc, a sector is the smallest memory unit.
 
• A sector on a magnetic disc or optical disc is a subdivision of a track in computer disc storage.
 
• Each sector of a hard disc drive (HDD) or a CD-ROM or DVD-ROM holds a defined amount of user-accessible data, typically 512 bytes for HDDs and 2048 bytes for CD-ROMs and DVD-ROMs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• A read/write head, often known as an RW head, is a device located on a hard drive's arm.
 
• A vector is an abstract data type that is used to describe attributes with both magnitude and direction (as opposed to a scalar that only has magnitude).
 
• The delivery of various services over the Internet is known as cloud computing.

 
• Sector is the smallest physical storage unit on the disk.
 
• Its size is 512 bytes in general.
 
• Sector is the subdivision of a track on a magnetic disc or optical disk.

questions.question: Which among the following features enables computers to perform multiple tasks at the same time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Versatility**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Versatility** is the feature that enables computers to perform multiple tasks simultaneously.
 
• This characteristic allows computers to execute diverse operations such as running applications, managing processes, and handling data efficiently.
 
• **Versatility** ensures the computer can adapt to different tasks and requirements based on user needs.
 
• It forms the basis for multitasking, which is a crucial aspect of modern computing systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diligence:** Computers do not suffer from fatigue or boredom and can work continuously without losing efficiency.
 
• **Automation:** Computers can execute predefined instructions automatically without manual intervention once programmed.
 
• **Speed:** Computers process data and instructions at an incredible speed, far beyond human capabilities.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: Exabyte > Petabyte > Terabyte > Gigabyte**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **In terms of data storage size, the hierarchy is as follows:**
 
• **Gigabyte (GB):** A gigabyte is approximately 1 billion bytes or 10⁹ bytes.
 
• **Terabyte (TB):** A terabyte is approximately 1 trillion bytes or 10¹² bytes.
 
• **Petabyte (PB):** A petabyte is approximately 1 quadrillion bytes or 10¹⁵ bytes.
 
• **Exabyte (EB):** An exabyte is approximately 1 quintillion bytes or 10¹⁸ bytes.
 
• **The correct sequence from largest to smallest is: Exabyte > Petabyte > Terabyte > Gigabyte.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other units of data storage include:**
 
• **Kilobyte (KB):** Approximately 1,000 bytes or 10³ bytes.
 
• **Megabyte (MB):** Approximately 1 million bytes or 10⁶ bytes.
 
• **Zettabyte (ZB):** Approximately 1 sextillion bytes or 10²¹ bytes.
 
• **Yottabyte (YB):** Approximately 1 septillion bytes or 10²⁴ bytes.
 
• The sequence provided in Option 1 aligns with the correct order of data storage sizes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a temporary storage media?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RAM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a type of computer memory that can be accessed randomly. It is the most common type of memory found in computers and other devices, such as printers.
 
• **RAM** is considered a temporary storage media because it only retains data as long as the computer is powered on. Once the computer is turned off, all data stored in RAM is lost.
 
• It is used to store data that is being currently used or processed by the CPU, allowing for quick read and write access.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pen Drives**: Also known as USB flash drives, these are portable storage devices that use flash memory to store data permanently. They are not considered temporary storage.
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)**: This is non-volatile memory used to store firmware or software that is rarely changed. Data in ROM remains even when the computer is turned off.
 
• **Hard Disk**: This is a type of permanent storage media used to store data long-term. It retains data even when the computer is turned off.

questions.question: _______ option determines the distance of the paragraph from either the left or the right margin.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** In**dent__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An indent increases the distance between the side of a paragraph and the left or right margin. Indented paragraphs appear to have different margin settings. Word provides a variety of indents to emphasize paragraphs in a document. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paragraph formatting** is a change in the **format** of the **text** that affects an entire **paragraph** or is **different** from other **paragraphs** in a document. **Paragraphs** in a word processing document or on a web page can have **paragraph formatting** applied to them, including font type, font size, highlighting, and indentation.
 
• **Mail merging** means to plug data from an address table into form letters, e-**mail** messages, envelopes, address labels, or a directory (a list or catalogue, for example).
 
• **Borders** are rules you can add to any or all of the four sides of a paragraph. **Shading** is the colour or artistic design you use as the background for a paragraph. **Borders and shading** are formatting tools for enhancing text, paragraphs, table cells, or frames.
 
• **Right alignment** or **right** justify is text or page formatting that aligns text along the **right** side of a page or containing element.

questions.question: ________ is a type of virus that could affect files in MS Word.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Macro virus__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• A macro virus is a type of virus that could be stored in macros.
 
• Not only MS Word, but the macro virus also affects all the MS Office suite applications or any ActiveX controls that have macros in them.
 
• Although macros are used to automate frequently used tasks, they do pose a security threat. Attackers are likely to install malicious software through macros and hence they must not be enabled unless absolutely necessary.
 
• The macro virus spreads rapidly via shared documents, either offline or as email attachments, downloading infected files etc. It is platform-independent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• A trojan is a type of malware that enters the system silently through an email attachment or when downloaded something from an untrusted source. 

 
 
• They are hard to detect because they appear as trusted applications.
 
 
 
• The worm is a standalone computer virus that replicates itself and spreads throughout the system. They use the computer as a host and infect the other parts.
 
• Malware is malicious software that is designed to disrupt the normal functions of a computer or a server. They leak confidential information or gain unauthorized access.
